pages.title: Microneedling information
pages.content:
Microneedling: full treatment information

Dear client,

You have chosen to have a microneedling treatment. This detailed information document explains the treatment, possible risks, side effects and the aftercare required.

What is microneedling?

Microneedling is a minimally invasive cosmetic procedure in which fine needles (0.5–2.5 mm) create controlled micro-injuries in the skin. These stimulate the skin's natural healing processes and boost the production of collagen and elastin. The procedure is also known as collagen induction therapy (CIT).

How it works

The fine needles pass through the outer layer of the skin (epidermis) and reach the dermis. This creates microscopic channels that trigger the following processes:

  • Wound-healing response: The skin activates its natural repair mechanisms
  • Collagen production: New collagen fibres form and improve the skin's texture
  • Elastin formation: Skin elasticity increases
  • Improved circulation: The supply of nutrients to the skin is optimised
  • Active ingredient penetration: Skincare products can penetrate deeper into the skin

Areas of application

  • Acne scars: Improvement of atrophic (indented) scars
  • Fine lines and wrinkles: Smoothing of superficial signs of ageing
  • Enlarged pores: A more refined complexion
  • Hyperpigmentation: Lightening of pigmentation spots
  • Stretch marks: Improved skin texture
  • General skin rejuvenation: Better texture and radiance
  • Scars: Various types of scar tissue

Treatment procedure in detail

  1. Preparation: Thorough cleansing and disinfection of the skin
  2. Numbing: Application of a numbing cream (30–45 minutes to take effect)
  3. Treatment: Systematic microneedling with sterile needles
  4. Active ingredients: Application of serums (hyaluronic acid, vitamin C, etc.)
  5. Soothing: Cooling, calming mask
  6. Aftercare: Application of skincare products and sun protection

Treatment parameters

  • Needle length: 0.5–2.5 mm, depending on the skin concern
  • Treatment time: 30–90 minutes, depending on the area
  • Number of sessions: 3–6 treatments for optimal results
  • Interval: 4–6 weeks between sessions

Possible side effects and risks

Common, normal reactions (>50%):

  • Redness and swelling for 24–72 hours
  • A feeling of tightness and mild pain
  • Pinpoint bleeding during the treatment
  • Increased skin sensitivity
  • Light flaking after 3–5 days

Occasional side effects (5–20%):

  • More pronounced swelling (especially around the eyes)
  • Small bruises (petechiae)
  • Itching during healing
  • Temporary hyperpigmentation
  • Dryness and flaking

Rare complications (1–5%):

  • Infections (bacterial, viral, fungal)
  • Allergic reactions to active ingredients
  • Reactivation of herpes simplex (cold sores)
  • Post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation
  • Scarring (very rare when performed correctly)

Very rare risks (<1%):

  • Permanent changes in pigmentation
  • Granuloma formation
  • Transmission of pathogens (if hygiene standards are not met)

Contraindications (treatment not possible)

  • Pregnancy and breastfeeding
  • Active skin infections in the treatment area
  • Active acne with inflamed lesions
  • Open wounds or eczema
  • Isotretinoin use within the last 6 months
  • Tendency to keloids or abnormal scarring
  • Blood clotting disorders
  • Immunosuppression
  • Skin cancer in the treatment area

Relative contraindications (extra caution required)

  • Diabetes mellitus
  • Autoimmune diseases
  • Use of blood thinners
  • Rosacea or very sensitive skin
  • Recent sun exposure or tanning
  • Use of retinol/acids within the last 7 days

Important dos and don'ts

Before the treatment (1–2 weeks):

  • Do not use retinol or acid-based products
  • Avoid sun exposure and sunbeds
  • No hair removal in the treatment area
  • If you are prone to cold sores: preventive medication
  • Drink plenty of fluids and eat a healthy diet

After the treatment (1–2 weeks):

  • 24–48 hours: no make-up on the treated area
  • 48 hours: no sauna, exercise or heavy sweating
  • 1 week: no retinol or acid-based products
  • 2 weeks: consistent sun protection (SPF 50+)
  • Use gentle, fragrance-free skincare products
  • Do not scratch or rub the skin
  • Drink plenty of water

Results and expectations

The results of microneedling develop gradually:

  • Immediately: A subtle glow thanks to improved circulation
  • 1–2 weeks: First improvement in skin texture
  • 4–6 weeks: Noticeable new collagen formation
  • 3–6 months: Full results after a course of treatments

Realistic expectations:

  • 30–70% improvement in skin texture
  • 25–50% reduction in scarring
  • Refined pores
  • Increased skin elasticity
  • A more even skin tone

Costs and treatment plan

Costs vary depending on the treatment area and the number of sessions. For optimal results, we recommend:

  • 3–6 treatments at intervals of 4–6 weeks
  • Maintenance treatments every 6–12 months
  • Individual adjustments based on how your skin responds

Alternative treatment options

  • Chemical peels
  • Laser resurfacing
  • Radiofrequency treatments
  • IPL (intense pulsed light)
  • Injectable treatments (fillers, Botox)
  • Surgical procedures
  • No treatment

Emergency contact: If you experience serious side effects or complications, contact us immediately or go to your nearest emergency department.

pages.title: Confirmation and next steps
pages.content:
Thank you for your detailed information!

Your details and your consent to the microneedling treatment have been recorded in full and will be treated confidentially.

Important information for your appointment:

1 week before the treatment:

  • Do not use retinol or acid-based products
  • Avoid sun exposure and sunbeds
  • No hair removal in the treatment area
  • If you are prone to cold sores: discuss preventive medication

On the day of treatment:

  • Arrive with no make-up on the treatment area
  • Wear comfortable clothing
  • Allow enough time (approx. 60–90 minutes)
  • If you feel unwell or have skin problems, reschedule your appointment

After the treatment:

  • No make-up for 24–48 hours
  • No sauna or intense exercise for 48 hours
  • No retinol or acid-based products for 1 week
  • Consistent sun protection (SPF 50+) for 2 weeks
  • Use gentle, fragrance-free skincare products

Treatment plan:

For optimal results, we recommend 3–6 treatments at intervals of 4–6 weeks. Your next appointment will be planned after the first treatment, based on how your skin responds.

Emergency contact:

If you experience serious side effects or complications, contact us immediately or go to your nearest emergency department.

We look forward to treating you professionally and safely!

pages.title: Permanent make-up information
pages.content:
Permanent make-up treatment information

Dear client,

You have chosen to have a permanent make-up treatment. This document explains the treatment process, possible risks and aftercare.

The treatment method

With permanent make-up, special colour pigments approved for use on humans are introduced into the upper layers of the skin (epidermis/dermis) using fine needles. Depending on factors such as skin type, lifestyle and sun exposure, the result usually lasts 1–5 years. A touch-up session after 4–6 weeks is usually needed for the best result.

Treatment process

The treatment involves the following steps:

  1. Consultation and colour selection
  2. Pre-drawing of the desired shape
  3. Local numbing of the treatment area (optional)
  4. Implantation of the colour pigments
  5. Final care and aftercare advice

Possible side effects and risks

  • Normal reactions: Redness, slight swelling, a mild burning sensation and tightness for 1–2 days.
  • Rare side effects: Severe swelling, infections, allergic reactions to colour pigments or anaesthetics, temporary blistering.
  • Long-term risks: Colour changes, uneven fading, an asymmetrical appearance, scarring.

Aftercare

Correct aftercare is essential for the best result:

  • Protect the treated areas from sun, sunbeds, saunas and chlorinated water for 7–10 days
  • Avoid touching the area and do not scratch, even if it itches
  • No peels, AHA (fruit acid) or retinol products for at least 2 weeks
  • After eyeliner treatment, only use an eyelash curler once the area has fully healed
  • Attend the recommended touch-up session after 4–6 weeks

Important information

  • The final result is only visible after healing and any touch-up session
  • Immediately after the treatment, the colour looks much more intense and darker
  • No guarantee can be given for the exact colour development and longevity
  • If you are not satisfied with the result, a correction may be needed

pages.title: Lash extension information
pages.content:
Lash extension information

Dear client,

You have chosen to have lash extensions. This document explains the treatment process, possible risks and the aftercare required.

Treatment process

During a lash extension treatment, synthetic lashes are attached one by one to your natural lashes using a special adhesive. Depending on the look you want, the treatment takes around 1.5 to 2.5 hours. For optimal adhesion, please arrive with clean lashes that are free of oil and make-up.

Possible risks and side effects

  • Allergic reactions: In rare cases, the adhesive used can cause allergic reactions. At the first signs of an allergy (severe redness, swelling, itching), please contact us immediately.
  • Eye irritation: Your eyes may become slightly irritated during the treatment. This should settle quickly afterwards.
  • Damage to natural lashes: Incorrect application or improper care can damage your natural lashes.

Aftercare and care instructions

  • Avoid contact with water, steam and oily substances for 24–48 hours after the treatment.
  • Do not use oil-based products around the eyes.
  • Avoid rubbing your eyes and touching your lashes too often.
  • Do not use an eyelash curler or waterproof mascara.
  • Brush your lashes regularly with a clean spoolie.
  • Try to sleep on your back to avoid putting pressure on the lashes.
  • For the best result, we recommend an infill every 2–3 weeks.

How long they last

How long lash extensions last varies from person to person and depends on your natural lash cycle, your skin type and how you look after them. On average, they last 4–6 weeks. Regular infill appointments (every 2–3 weeks) help the result last longer.

pages.title: Nail design information
pages.content:
Nail enhancement information

Dear client,

You have chosen to have nail enhancements. This document explains the treatment process, possible risks and aftercare.

Treatment process

The nail enhancement treatment involves the following steps:

  1. Preparing the natural nails (shortening, filing, removing cuticles)
  2. Buffing the nail surface
  3. Applying tips (for extensions) or nail forms
  4. Applying the enhancement material (gel, acrylic, etc.)
  5. Curing under UV or LED light (for gel)
  6. Shaping and filing the nails
  7. Sealing and applying colour/design

Possible risks and side effects

  • Allergic reactions: In rare cases, the materials used can cause allergies.
  • Nail bed irritation: Irritation can occur if the products are applied or removed incorrectly.
  • Weakening of the natural nails: The natural nails can become thinner and more sensitive, especially after incorrect removal or frequent changes.
  • Nail infections: Poor hygiene or damage to the nails can lead to infections.

Aftercare and care instructions

  • Wear gloves when doing housework involving water or chemicals.
  • Use cuticle oil regularly to care for your natural nails and cuticles.
  • Do not use your nails as tools or expose them to excessive pressure.
  • If a nail is damaged, please visit the salon promptly to have it repaired.
  • To keep your nails looking their best, we recommend an infill every 3–4 weeks.
  • If you notice signs of infection or an allergic reaction, please see a doctor straight away.

Removal

Artificial nails should always be removed professionally. Snapping or peeling them off can damage the natural nail. Ideally, come back to us for removal.

pages.title: Laser hair removal information
pages.content:
Laser hair removal information

Dear client,

You have chosen to have permanent hair reduction with a laser. This document explains the procedure, possible risks and aftercare.

How laser hair removal works

During laser hair removal, pulses of light are directed at the skin. The melanin (pigment) in the hair absorbs the light, creating heat that destroys the hair follicles. Only hairs in the growth phase can be treated, and at any given time only around 20% of hairs are in this phase, so several treatments at intervals of 4–8 weeks are needed.

Possible risks and side effects

  • Common, temporary reactions: Redness, slight swelling and a warm feeling similar to sunburn for 1–3 days.
  • Less common side effects: Blistering, superficial burns, temporary hyper- or hypopigmentation (darkening or lightening of the skin).
  • Rare complications: Scarring, permanent changes in pigmentation, infection, reactivation of herpes (cold sores).

Important information before the treatment

  • No tanning (neither sun nor sunbed) in the treatment area for 4 weeks before the treatment.
  • Hair in the treatment area should be 1–2 mm long (shave approx. 1–3 days before the treatment).
  • For at least 4 weeks before the treatment, do not use hair removal methods that remove the root (waxing, epilating, threading).
  • Avoid using self-tanner or heavily fragranced products in the treatment area.

Aftercare

  • For 48 hours after the treatment: no hot baths, sauna, strenuous physical activity or swimming pools.
  • For 14 days after the treatment: consistent sun protection (SPF 50+) on the treated area.
  • If redness or swelling occurs, cool the area and use soothing, fragrance-free products.
  • Treated hairs may fall out 2–3 weeks after the treatment; this is normal.

Results and expectations

Results of laser hair removal vary from person to person and depend on factors such as skin type, hair colour and hormonal status. Optimal results usually require 6–10 treatments. A permanent reduction of 70–90% of hair is realistic, but 100% hair-free skin cannot be guaranteed. Hormonal changes can lead to new hair growth.
